C8 Chevy Corvette Z06 Drags R35 Nissan GT-R, One Driver Hits a 7.96s Pass and Another the Barrier
16 photos
Photo: Wheels / YouTube
The videographer behind the ' Wheels ' channel on YouTube usually dwells around The Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway or MRP (Mission Raceway Park, aka Thunder by the River, in British Columbia, Canada), but on this particular occasion they want to show us something from BMP – aka Bradenton Motorsports Park in Florida, all over again.
First, let’s meet the contestants: in the left lane sits a dark gray C8 Chevrolet Corvette Z06 with a full aerodynamic package and what look like aftermarket tires and wheels. The other driver has an ‘import’ versus the domestic representative from GM, a thoroughly modified R35 Nissan GT-R sports car. It’s a classic case of mid-engine versus the front-engine RWD recipe, so let’s find out who prevails.
These two feisty rivals were present at BMP, most likely for the FL2K event, and they were surrounded by teammates and fans; that’s for sure. They took their time setting up the perfect start position, but when the green light was on, it was pretty clear that only one of them was actually paying attention. As such, one of the contestants took a decisive advantage over their rival and went home victorious with a spectacular 7.96s pass at more than 173 mph.
The other one was far behind, on the other hand, with a result of 10.58s at just 104 mph. Actually, for the latter, the scoreboard was of no consequence because more important things happened during the run : the runner-up tried to start catching up to its rival, or something bad happened mechanically, because the car started skidding away from the ideal trajectory and impacted the concrete barrier without much input from the driver, who only hit the brakes right before the impact.
Nobody knows exactly what happened there; maybe there was an oil slip or something like that, or a mechanical issue, but one thing is for sure – that car needs extensive repairs now, as it even lost a rear wheel in the aftermath of the impact. Hopefully, nobody was hurt, and only the driver’s ego got bruised. Anyway, we didn’t want to spoil the fun of watching who’s who, so let’s check out the video embedded below; it’s only two minutes long.
Also, you might want to check out the comments section, too; there’s even more drama over there than across the tarmac of the quarter-mile dragstrip! Anyway, the C8 Chevrolet Corvette, unlike the R35 Nissan GT-R, is the only one alive and well in terms of production, as the Japanese sports car went on hiatus while Nissan decides what to do next with it.
Meanwhile, the C8 iteration of America’s sports car is fine and dandy, offering, for the 2027 model year, a new base V8 engine with 535 hp and 520 lb-ft of torque for the Stingray and Grand Sport, plus the Grand Sport X in combination with the ZR1X’s electrified setup.
